note: Audit 539228-c1/539228-s1: Included: 539228-s1 is this article's own ablation experiment (Au foil in 30 mL aqueous GO suspension, 532 nm second harmonic, 8 ns, 10 Hz, 15 min, four stated fluences 5.3/7.9/10.5/13.2 J/cm2), same medium class as the claim (colloid: graphene-oxide colloid in deionized water), same material Au and a comparable size quantity (TEM geometric-diameter mean). Assessed unassessable rather than direct: the series has only two points, at 10.5 and 13.2 J/cm2, and both carry the identical TEM value 30.0 nm. Those are not independent per-setting size measurements - the article reports exactly one size, 'the small Au nanoparticles of a diameter around ~30 nm are anchored on to the surface of the GO' (p.5, section 3.3), and names no fluence for it, while the two lower-fluence experiments (5.3 and 7.9 J/cm2, experiments 541119 and 541129) are excluded as no_size. The flat shape (30.0 vs 30.0, difference 0) is therefore a property of one fluence-unattributed text value carried by two experiments, not an observation that the size does not change with fluence; scoring the directionless claim 'affects' against it would manufacture a disagreement the text does not support. The claim's own stated evidence is also not a size series: the p.4 sentence sits in the UV-Vis section, where the measured quantities are the absorbance spectra and the ~526 nm SPR band, and no size value per fluence is reported anywhere in the article.; caveats: Only 2 of the 4 tested fluences have any size record; the lower two (5.3 and 7.9 J/cm2) are excluded as no_size, so the series covers 10.5-13.2 J/cm2 while the claim spans 5.3-13.2 J/cm2. Both points reproduce the same single text statement (~30 nm), so they are not independent evidence and a two-point series can only be flat or a single step. Point errors are the model fallback (0.10/0.20 x 30 nm): the snapshot stores no SD and no particles_counted, and the article reports no size uncertainty. The claim gives no direction, so agreement would require any non-flat shape. The article states no pulse energy in mJ, no power and no intensity, so the fluence values cannot be cross-checked from the text.
